scorecard.note: Specify clear, simple visuals that are easily readable on a phone screen.

storyboard.ears: Most of the bugs crawling around you have never even been given a name.
Roughly eight out of every ten animal species are insects, so the animal kingdom is mostly bugs, and we are the small minority.
storyboard.eyes: substance: drawers of pinned insects; cause: Data pulls each drawer of the cabinet open by its handle, eight full of bugs and two of everything else
storyboard.evidence: Smithsonian Institution / Royal Entomological Society | Insects as a share of all known animal species | https://www.si.edu/spotlight/buginfo/bugnos | 2026-08-09

storyboard.ears: Beetles alone have about 1.5 million species, while mammals and birds together are a tiny fraction of that. Bugs win by a landslide.
storyboard.evidence: Stork (2018), Annual Review of Entomology; IUCN / BirdLife International species counts | Estimated beetle species vs. total mammal and bird species | https://www.annualreviews.org/doi/10.1146/annurev-ento-020117-043348 | 2026-08-09

storyboard.ears: We've named about one in five insect species scientists think exist. That means most bugs out there have never even had a name.
storyboard.evidence: Annual Reviews / peer-reviewed entomology research | Insect species described so far vs. estimated to actually exist | https://www.annualreviews.org/doi/10.1146/annurev-ento-020117-043348 | 2026-08-09

storyboard.ears: Most bugs are still unnamed, so we barely know who we share this planet with.
